confirmed.title: Building interiors keep the exterior window glow instead of DFU's WindowStyle.Disabled (black)

Port: interiorContext.js:120 uploads window masks via uploadRecord (dataPipeline.js:89-91); drawMesh binds them (renderer.js:1578) times the global _windowEmission (renderer.js:1114-1115), which is only ever day/night/fog: main.js:67 boots it 'day'; world.js:3295 / exterior.js:1607 write it only in exterior frames (world.js:3070 modal return exits first); worldModes' interior block (:2779-2796) never calls setWindowEmission; WINDOW_STYLES (windowEmission.js:8-13) has no disabled entry.
confirmed.consequence: Inside every shop/tavern/house, window glass glows pale blue by day and amber at night where DFU/classic show unlit glass; contradicts the port's own bible (Rendering-Arc R2 note: 'emission stays dark (Disabled)').

confirmed.title: Dispatcher's Day window style overrides the ?interior scene's documented dark emission
confirmed.claim: main.js:67 runs renderer.setWindowEmission(windowEmissionRGB(params.get('window') || 'day')) BEFORE routing (the ?interior route is line 68), overwriting the renderer's black boot value (renderer.js:468). interior.js:28-30 documents the DFU law it relies on - 'SetClimate with WindowStyle.Disabled - emission stays dark here by default' - and neither interior.js nor interiorContext.js ever calls setWindowEmission, so 'by default' meant the renderer's boot state, which the dispatcher line defeats. The standalone-scene slice of the previous finding: the port disagrees with its own comment one import away.

confirmed.title: Four BEAST_DESIGNS entries quote wrong ENEMY_BASICS level/damage

confirmed.title: resolvePaperdollRecord/isCloak have no src caller; law duplicated inline

confirmed.title: Wraith design damage [10,45] contradicts EnemyBasics MinDamage 20
confirmed.claim: undeadBody.js:467 gives the Wraith design 'damage: [10, 45]' in a file whose sibling entries cite ENEMY_BASICS as source (e.g. Zombie :112). confirmed.title: Silenced touch-caster re-arms melee timer: reset happens before the silence gate
confirmed.claim: DFU DoTouchSpell resets the melee timer only after its whole condition passes, ending with SetReadySpell (EnemyMotor.cs:621-628), which returns false when silenced (EntityEffectManager.cs:315 SilenceCheck) - a silenced enemy's DoTouchSpell fails without touching MeleeTimer and its ordinary melee fires normally. The port's EnemyCaster.update resets attack.meleeTimer (enemyCasting.js:114) BEFORE returning the touch decision; the silence gate runs later in castEnemySpell (:159) and returns false with the timer already re-armed 1.5-3s. The arm re-fires every time the timer hits 0, usually beating the melee decision (which needs a classic tick plus the DFRandom roll on that exact frame).
confirmed.consequence: Silence a touch-casting enemy (ghost, Frost Daedra, healer) and in the port it stands in melee range mostly not attacking - its melee timer perpetually re-armed by failed casts - where DFU's silenced caster falls back to normal melee attacks.

confirmed.title: canAccessLibrary ported but library bookshelves are absent entirely

confirmed.title: Duplicate hudCtx toggleRest key: complete outdoor rest path dead, crippled twin runs
confirmed.claim: hudCtx defines toggleRest twice (:1922 outdoorRestDeps path, :1932 toggleExteriorRest); the later wins, so the full S40 path (outdoorRestDeps :1377: areEnemiesNearby({resting:true}), tickQuests, endLines) is dead code. The live exteriorRestDeps (:960): (a) enemiesNearby = activeCount()>0, but GameManager.cs:684-702 skips a foe that cannot see you beyond 12 units - any live guard anywhere refuses rest (TEXT 354); (b) no tickQuests - a rested night runs zero quest ticks (DaggerfallRestWindow.cs:376-379); (c) TEXT.RSC reader keyed textLines (:963), not the endLines createRestDeps composes (shared.js:1177). Pins restwhere:170 / restlodging:589 each match one arm and miss the shadowing.

confirmed.title: Same duplicate toggleRest key in ?exterior: rest blocks on any guard, loses end text
confirmed.claim: exterior.js:1016 toggleRest (outdoorRestDeps :636, areEnemiesNearby(cityGuards.guards,{resting:true}) + endLines) is shadowed by :1027 toggleExteriorRest, so every Rest key/panel runs exteriorRestDeps (:928): enemiesNearby is activeCount()>0 - exactly what the dead deps' comment (:643-647) warns 'would block sleep for good the moment one guard spawned anywhere in town' - and the TEXT.RSC reader is keyed textLines (:931), not endLines, so RestWindow._end gets null and closes silently. DFU gates rest open via AreEnemiesNearby(true) (DaggerfallUI.cs:652) and hourly via the same resting variant (DaggerfallRestWindow.cs:403): an unaware enemy blocks only within 12 units.

confirmed.title: Dungeon hosts never run the 8-hour enemy-alert decay
confirmed.claim: decayEnemyAlert's only caller in src/ is shared.createPlayerTicker.tick (shared.js:746), and neither dungeon host builds a ticker: dungeonContext's frame body calls tickPlayerMinutes directly (:2100) and its rest advance uses claimMagicRounds/runMagicRoundsFor (:953-963); nothing calls decayEnemyAlert. DFU decays the alert in PlayerEntity.Update in every context (PlayerEntity.cs:381-384). The port raises it whenever a foe has the player in sight (:2233) and clears it only when the detecting foe dies (:1847), so underground it only goes up. Its sole consumer is the dungeon resting spawn roll (encounters.js rollDungeon: alert -> 1/36 per rested minute; no alert -> never).
confirmed.consequence: Resting in a dungeon 8+ hours after last enemy contact (or when the sighting foe was not killed): DFU rolls no interruption spawns; the port rolls 1-in-36 per rested minute forever, breaking long dungeon rests with spawns classic would not mint.

confirmed.title: Modal RMB mousedown lacks window-up gate: inventory Remove gesture casts readied spell
confirmed.claim: worldModes' global mousedown (:3402-3404) and mouseup (:3399-3401) feed the modal attack sink on e.button===2 alone. Every sibling gates on a window up: dungeon.js:195 ('a right-click on a window is the window's (the remove gesture), never a swing'), world.js:2062, exterior.js:1168. The sink runs magic.interceptAttack(true) first (dungeonContext.js:1475-1483; interior arm :3391), which latches pendingClickCast when a spell is readied (hostMagic.js:489-492); interior mode fires it the same frame (firePending :2803 runs with the overlay up), dungeon mode fires on window close. DFU windows pause the game on push (UserInterfaceManager.cs:179-185); a window click never reaches the cast.
confirmed.consequence: With a spell readied, right-clicking an item (Remove gesture) in a modal interior/dungeon inventory or trade window silently casts it - magicka spent, missile fired - where the standalone dungeon and both exterior slots swallow the click.

confirmed.title: Dungeon fall damage never flashes the screen; the other three hosts do
confirmed.claim: dungeonContext's own fall arm (reportActivity :2718-2723 - fed by both dungeon hosts, dungeon.js:418 and worldModes.js:2685) does hurtPlayer + FallDamage sound only; its 'ShowPlayerDamage screen flash pends the HUD arc (flagged)' comment is stale - flashPlayerDamage exists and this file calls it for arrows (:1701) and melee (:1945). DFU's ApplyPlayerFallDamage calls RemoveHealth (PlayerHealth.cs:49-58), whose first act is ShowPlayerDamage.Flash() (:36-38), so every damaging fall flashes. shared.applyFallLanding, the arm the other three hosts use (shared.js:531-547), calls flashPlayerDamage for this exact reason; the wave39 test pin covers shared.js and the enemy-blow sites but not this arm.

confirmed.title: Exterior Detect feeds pass no loot pool though dropped piles and corpses exist above ground

The HUD comments justify it as 'no loot PILES above ground (FLAGGED)' (world.js:3542-3545, exterior.js:1837-1839), but both hosts mount createDroppedLoot (player drops become world piles, world.js:819 / exterior.js:564) and both have lootable corpse containers (cityGuards/exteriorFoes lootTargets). confirmed.title: Painting identity + info macros unported; paintings are purchasable and show raw %-macros
confirmed.claim: DFU: DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:571 seeds message=Random.Range(0,65536) for Paintings; InitPaintingInfo (DaggerfallUnityItemMCP.cs:42-65) does DFRandom.srand(message), rand()%180 for file/record, GetPaintingRecordPart random_range_inclusive draws, and %sub/%adj/%pp1/%pp2/%an each burn/draw rand() (all five registered in MacroHelper.cs). confirmed.title: StockHouseContainer unported: private house containers are permanently empty
confirmed.claim: DFU stocks a house container on first access (PlayerActivate.cs:911-913 -> StockHouseContainer): picks an item group from the privatePropertyItems tables by container model + building type, then mints items in a loop with a halving continue chance gated by DFRandom.rand()%100 > continueChance (DaggerfallLoot.cs:369-371) - DaggerfallLoot's only DFRandom draw. The port identifies house containers verbatim (systems/containers.js) but interiorContext.js:127-130 declares private furniture starts EMPTY, worldModes.js:2409-2417 transferAll()s the always-empty c.items, and no port code stocks them; the privatePropertyItems tables do not exist in src/.

confirmed.title: Human-enemy gender roll substitutes Math.random for DFU's shared DFRandom draw
confirmed.claim: DFU decides an unspecified-gender human enemy's gender with the shared LCG: GetTextureArchive does DFRandom.random_range(0,2)==0 -> Male else Female (DaggerfallMobileUnit.cs:626), consuming one shared-stream draw per such enemy. The port rolls the same 50/50 with Math.random at the hosts (dungeonContext.js:924, also :531/:596 via MobileUnit ctor arg, exteriorFoes.js:86), consuming no shared draw.
confirmed.consequence: One shared-stream draw per unspecified-gender human enemy is skipped vs DFU; DFU's draw rides the unseeded, frame-cadence-dependent stream position (nondeterministic between sessions) and the 50/50 distribution is identical, so no reproducible sequence breaks - negligible observable impact.

confirmed.title: forceExitToExterior drops the mode overlay without dispose - isResting latches for the session
confirmed.claim: forceExitToExterior (worldModes.js:3937-3948) nulls interiorOverlay raw and destroys dungeonCtx without disposing its activeOverlay. RestWindow raises entity.isResting on construction (restWindow.js:96, shared.js:1145) and clears it only in _close/dispose (:107-125); DFU always clears via OnPop (:284). Path: rest -> sub-tick runs tickQuests (restSession.js:388-404) -> TeleportPc (actions.js:1818-1819) -> respawnPlayerAtSite (world.js:2386-2395) -> _respawnAtSite (world.js:1549-1550) calls forceExitToExterior synchronously -> the open RestWindow is discarded, setResting(false) never runs. worldModes.js:4007-4012 documents this exact failure class; this door missed the fix.
confirmed.consequence: After a quest teleport lands mid-rest, playerEntity.isResting stays true until reload: passive fatigue never drains again (worldTick.js:422) and held enchanted items degrade at 60/round instead of 4 (enchantments.js:317) - 15x item destruction, for the rest of the session.

confirmed.title: Exterior corpse batches never culled, freed, or cleared on teleport - unbounded growth
confirmed.claim: Both exterior pools keep every corpse forever: exteriorFoes' splice spares corpses (:401), the cull (:286) skips dead foes (:252), and corpseBatches (:60/:214/:486) has no removal path - batches() draws every corpse every frame. cityGuards.js is identical (:95/:290/:445; :248-256 says guards[] cannot be pruned). The teleport core (world.js:1478-1500) never touches either pool. DFU tracks exterior corpse markers as loose objects (GameObjectHelper.cs:839) and destroys them when out of range or on any teleport (CollectLooseObjects :1040-1055; ClearStreamingWorld :993 from InitWorld :584). The port ported that law for player drops (droppedLoot.collectPixel cites :1040-1052) but not for corpses.
confirmed.consequence: Every kill permanently adds a VAO+buffers and an array entry drawn every frame; corpses from towns you fast-travelled away from still render and probe loot AABBs. GPU memory and draw time grow without bound over a session.

confirmed.title: dungeonContext.destroy() skips the dead-mark on dropped piles; spawnCorpse lacks a context-alive guard
confirmed.claim: droppedLoot's async mount guards only on pile.dead (droppedLoot.js:54) and every other removal site sets dead first (:93/:111/:129/:167 - protocol documented at :45-53). dungeonContext.destroy (:3066-3069) frees batches and clears _piles WITHOUT setting dead, so a pile dropped just before exiting whose texture is still warming mints a batch onto an orphan after destroy ran. Same class: spawnCorpse (:1449-1473) awaits getTexture and guards only '!f.dead' (:1459), so a foe killed right before exit mints a corpse batch into the destroyed context's lists.
confirmed.consequence: One leaked GPU batch per exit-during-texture-warm (drop or first kill of an enemy type immediately before leaving). Rare, but violates the module's own documented ownership protocol.

confirmed.title: tryEnter's failure path leaks the fully built interior context
confirmed.claim: tryEnter builds the whole interior context (worldModes.js:2224 - GPU billboard batches plus voxelfolk race meshes) before computing the landing; a null landing throws 'no interior landing' (:2238) before interiorCtx is assigned, and both hosts only log it (world.js:3210, exterior.js:1538 catch -> console.error). Nothing calls ctx.destroy() on that path, so the build's GPU allocations are orphaned. In DFU a failed transition's objects still die with the Unity scene teardown; here the port owns every allocation and the error path drops them.
confirmed.consequence: A building whose interior yields no enter markers and no doors leaks its full interior GPU allocation on every E-press (repeatable - the door is not marked bad). Reachable only on degenerate interior data I could not confirm exists in the shipped set.

confirmed.title: audio.ensure guards its await with a boolean - second caller resolves before DAGGER.SND loads
confirmed.claim: AudioEngine.ensure sets this._booted = true and returns before 'await this.init(fetchBytes)' completes (audio.js:69-88), so a concurrent second caller's await resolves while enabled is still false and its immediate playOneShot/play3d calls silently drop. The sibling MusicService documents and fixed this exact race ('AUDIT 19 F1/F11... The flag is now the PROMISE... A guard set before its own async work is not idempotence, it is a race with a flag on it', music.js:39-54); the sound engine kept the boolean shape.
confirmed.consequence: One-shots requested between a first ensure starting and DAGGER.SND finishing are lost, not queued. Per-frame callers self-heal (torch loops retry on null handle), so impact today is marginal boot-window sound loss.

confirmed.title: Exterior quicksave saves no live enemies (encounter foes + city guards)
confirmed.claim: DFU's SaveData_v1 carries enemyData for every registered live enemy wherever the player stands (BuildSaveData :865, restored :1006), and SerializableStateManager.RestoreEnemyData (:404-425) re-instantiates each one from prefab on load (exterior handled by SerializableEnemy.cs:189-191). The port's worldQuickSave world half (world.js:1635-1641) carries only pixel/native coords/height/piles; exteriorFoes.foes and cityGuards.guards (live spell targets per world.js:1084) are saved nowhere, and worldQuickLoad restores only piles, then sets _lastEncMinutes to suppress spawn catch-up (world.js:1678).
confirmed.consequence: Quicksave during a wilderness ambush or guard pursuit and quickload: every attacker despawns with no catch-up spawn - a free escape from any exterior fight that DFU's save round-trips intact.

confirmed.title: Dungeon foe snapshot omits active effect bundles (instancedEffectBundles)
confirmed.claim: SerializableEnemy saves each enemy's instancedEffectBundles (:120) and restores them via RestoreInstancedBundleSaveData (:222). The port's foes ARE effect targets - applySpellToFoe (hostMagic.js:106-107) runs applySpell on foe.entity and effects.js pushes onto target.activeEffects (:519-547) - but collectWorld's per-foe record (dungeonContext.js:1745-1756) carries only health/dead/feet/yaw/items/hostile/encountered/magicka; f.entity.activeEffects is never snapshotted and applyWorld (:1768-1781) never restores it.
confirmed.consequence: Paralysis, continuous damage, soul trap marks, and every other timed effect on every dungeon enemy silently ends on quicksave+quickload: a paralyzed boss wakes, a burning foe stops burning - in DFU the bundles survive the load.

confirmed.title: applyWorld never removes live foes beyond the snapshot; rewound CreateFoe re-spawns duplicates
confirmed.claim: DFU's load rebuilds the scene and instantiates exactly the saved enemy set (RestoreEnemyData creates one object per saved record; enemies born after the save are gone with the rebuild). The port's applyWorld (dungeonContext.js:1768-1770) patches foes in place by index over w.foes only - a live foes[] entry at an index past the snapshot's length is left standing untouched. Meanwhile restoreSessionState rewinds CreateFoe's spawnCounter/lastSpawnTime (quest/actions.js:1980 saveShape), so the restored action's wave budget no longer accounts for the survivor.
confirmed.consequence: Quicksave, let a quest wave (create foe) spawn, quickload: the post-save wave stays alive AND the rewound CreateFoe counter spawns it again - duplicate quest foes after a backward load, where DFU's rebuild-from-save yields exactly the saved population.

confirmed.title: daedraSummonDay/daedraSummonIndex mutated on the entity but never saved or restored
confirmed.claim: DFU persists PlayerEntity.DaedraSummonDay and DaedraSummonIndex one-for-one (GetSaveData :164-165, RestoreSaveData :332-333). The port stores the coven's remembered daily roll on the same entity - daedraForSummoner mutates state.daedraSummonIndex/state.daedraSummonDay (daedraSummoning.js:109-111) and worldModes.js:1635 passes state: playerEntity - but ENTITY_FIELDS (save.js:30-58) omits both, so snapshotPlayer never writes them and restorePlayer neither restores nor clears them.
confirmed.consequence: The witch coven's daedra-of-the-day re-derives instead of restoring: reload from a fresh boot and the coven re-rolls (save-scum until the prince you want answers); an in-session backward load keeps the post-save roll instead of the saved one. DFU round-trips the roll exactly.

confirmed.title: Foe maxHealth (startingHealth) and fatigue not round-tripped
confirmed.claim: SerializableEnemy saves startingHealth (entity.MaxHealth, :109) and currentFatigue (:111) and restores both (:175 MaxHealth, :177 SetFatigue). The port's collectWorld saves only health/magicka; makeEnemyEntity re-rolls maxHealth with Math.random on every rebuild (characters/enemyEntity.js:80 rollEnemyClassMaxHealth, :85 Range(min,max+1)), and foe fatigue is live drained/restored state (dungeonContext.js:1109-1110 foe sinks) that applyWorld never touches.
confirmed.consequence: On a rebuild-then-restore load (standalone ?dungeon ?load path) each monster's max HP re-rolls, so restored health can exceed the new max and enemy toughness shifts across a load; on any in-session quickload a fatigue-drained foe keeps its live value instead of the saved one.

confirmed.title: Interior host cannot save at all (savingPrevented hardwired true)
confirmed.claim: DFU saves inside buildings: SerializablePlayer stores exteriorDoors + buildingDiscoveryData when IsPlayerInsideBuilding (:183-187) and SaveLoadManager.cs:1410-1418 restores the interior context on load. The port's interior mode wires the pause window with savingPrevented: () => true (worldModes.js:3560; 'You cannot save now.' per pauseWindow.js:192-195) and mounts no quickSave/quickLoad in its routeKey ctx, so F9 inside a building is a silent no-op. Flagged in-code as unbuilt (worldModes.js:3416-3419) - reported so the audit ledger carries the row; refuters should not treat it as an unknown regression.
confirmed.consequence: A player inside any shop, tavern, temple, or house cannot save the game; DFU saves anywhere. Progress since the last exterior/dungeon save is lost on a crash inside.

confirmed.title: Weapon drawn/sheathed state not in the envelope
confirmed.claim: DFU saves data.weaponDrawn (:175) and restores weaponManager.Sheathed = !data.weaponDrawn (:420). The port's sheath state lives on weaponRig.playerWeapon.sheathed in both saving hosts (world.js:892, dungeonContext.js:1482) but snapshotPlayer carries no field for it and neither host's quickLoad touches the rig.
confirmed.consequence: A save made with the weapon drawn always loads with it in the rig's default state - the player must re-draw after every load; DFU restores the drawn state.

confirmed.title: Player yaw, pitch, and crouch state not saved with position
confirmed.claim: PlayerPositionData_v1 carries yaw, pitch, and isCrouching (:212-214), restored by RestorePosition. The port saves only lastPlayerFeet (dungeonContext.js:2729) and restores via setPlayerPos(extras.position) (:2767) - a bare 3-vector; the world host's envelope (world.js:1636) likewise carries coordinates only. The port has crouch (player/motor.js P12) and mouselook yaw/pitch, so the state exists to lose.
confirmed.consequence: Every load resets facing to the motor default and stands the player up; a save made crouched in a 0.9-height crawlspace loads standing at that spot.

confirmed.title: FACTION_TYPE_INDIVIDUAL is 3 but FactionTypes.Individual is 4 (3 is Subgroup)
confirmed.claim: staticNpc.js:220 exports FACTION_TYPE_INDIVIDUAL = 3 and staticNpcName:209 tests fd.type === 3. DFU FactionFile.cs:537-538: Subgroup = 3, Individual = 4; StaticNPC.GetDisplayName (:319) tests type == Individual (4). The port's production faction dict agrees with DFU (src/formats/factionFile.js:17 Individual: 4; npcSession.js:62 same), so staticNpcName's check never matches a real Individual and instead matches Subgroup factions. Test pins (staticnpc.test.js:112 uses the constant; audit24_onehome.test.js:196 hardcodes type 3) restate the port, not the C#.
confirmed.consequence: A named individual (King Gothryd, type 4) clicked in a palace shows a random generated name instead of the faction's fixed name; an NPC whose faction is a Subgroup (type 3, e.g. a knightly order) is named with the faction's own name string.

verify.reason: DFU FactionFile.cs:537-538: Subgroup=3, Individual=4; StaticNPC.cs:319 tests type==(int)Individual(4). Port's staticNpc.js:220 sets FACTION_TYPE_INDIVIDUAL=3, used at :209 - checks Subgroup not Individual. Port's own faction dict and quest code (questMacros.js:321,365; actions.js:2340,2412) correctly use 4 elsewhere, confirming staticNpc.js is the outlier. Both cited test pins mock type:3 as 'individual', restating the bug.

confirmed.title: Static NPC generated names use the race's name bank; DFU always uses the region's
confirmed.claim: staticNpcName defaults bank = bankForRace(data.race) (staticNpc.js:211). DFU: SetRuntimeData sets npcData.nameBank = GetNameBankOfCurrentRegion() (StaticNPC.cs:309, always Breton/Redguard) and GetDisplayName calls FullName(npcData.nameBank, gender) (:325-326); TalkManager.cs:2848 uses the region bank too; nothing assigns a race bank. Both production callers omit nameBank (worldModes.js:976, 1364). The port knows the law for mobiles (world.js:506, exterior.js:1367 pass getNameBankOfRegion citing MobilePersonNPC.cs:214) and staticNpc.js:233 re-exports getNameBankOfRegion, but no static caller uses it. Factions without a race: line parse race 0 = Nord on both sides.
confirmed.consequence: Any interior static NPC whose derived race differs from the region race (incl. the Nord default on race-less factions) is named from the wrong bank - Nord '...sen' surnames in Breton/Redguard towns where DFU generates regional names.

verify.reason: DFU StaticNPC.cs:309 always sets npcData.nameBank = GetNameBankOfCurrentRegion() before GetDisplayName (:325-326) uses it - region-based, never race-based. Port's staticNpcName (staticNpc.js:206,211) defaults to bankForRace(data.race); its only two callers (worldModes.js:976,1364) never pass nameBank. Port already has getNameBankOfRegion wired for mobile NPCs (world.js:506) but never for static NPCs - an unported gap, not a departure.

confirmed.title: Guild-popup Talk seam builds staticNpcData without race lookups: race is always Nord there
confirmed.claim: talkToStaticNpcHere (worldModes.js:1361-1374, the GuildServicePopup Talk button / Spymaster dismissal) calls staticNpcData(pn, {...questSceneCtx(), buildingKey}); questSceneCtx returns only {mapId, locationIndex} (world.js:2808, exterior.js:1222-1225), so getFaction stays null and raceOfCurrentRegion defaults () => 0. raceFromFaction(fid!=0, null,...) then always yields Nord (staticNpc.js:139-141), and staticNpcName uses the Nord bank. The direct-click seam passes real lookups (questBridge.js:256-257; worldModes.js:890). DFU's GetRaceFromFaction (StaticNPC.cs:357-369) always has the live FactionData lookup and region fallback; the popup Talk reads the same StaticNPC.Data.
confirmed.consequence: The same NPC answers a different generated name through the popup's Talk button than through a direct click (same seed, different bank/draw pattern), and every NPC on that path is stamped race Nord.

verify.reason: worldModes.js:1363 calls staticNpcData(pn, {...questSceneCtx(), buildingKey}) with no getFaction/raceOfCurrentRegion, so raceFromFaction's fallback (staticNpc.js:139-141) always yields Nord. The direct-click seam (worldModes.js:890) instead uses questBridge.clickNpc, which adds npcRaceLookups() (questBridge.js:237-239,256-259) with real lookups off ctx.world - matching DFU's single unconditional GetRaceFromFaction (StaticNPC.cs:357-369). No test pin covers this omission.

confirmed.title: talkToStaticNPC gets the raw block record as data, so nameSeed reads 0 for every static NPC
confirmed.claim: worldModes.js:979 and :1366 pass { data: pn, ... } where pn is the block-person record (no nameSeed field; nothing in src/ writes pn.nameSeed - the derived npcData with the real seed is computed at :890/:1363 and used only for displayName). npcSession.talkToStaticNPC reads targetNPC?.data?.nameSeed ?? 0 (npcSession.js:467) = 0 always; worldModes.js:1021/:1370 likewise pass npcSeed: pn.nameSeed ?? 0 into openTalkWindow. DFU passes the StaticNPC whose .Data carries the derived nameSeed (TalkManager.cs:759, :770). The audit24_onehome.test.js:225 pin asserts the '{ data: pn, ... }' shape - it restates the port.
confirmed.consequence: castleNPCsSpokenTo is keyed by 0 (npcSession.js:564-573): the first castle NPC clicked consumes the only 25% work roll and no castle NPC can ever offer work after; talk-answer randomization is identical for every static NPC instead of per-person.

verify.reason: worldModes.js:979/1366 pass targetNPC={data:pn,...} where pn (from interiorPeople.js:30-48) has no nameSeed field; the real derived nameSeed is computed separately and used only for displayName. npcSession.js:467 reads targetNPC?.data?.nameSeed??0, always 0, so isCastleNpcOfferingQuest keys castleNPCsSpokenTo by 0 (npcSession.js:564-573) vs DFU's per-NPC targetNPC.Data.nameSeed (TalkManager.cs:769). audit24_onehome.test.js:225 pins the exact buggy shape.

confirmed.title: collectExteriorNpcs has no production caller: exterior static NPCs never exist
confirmed.claim: collectExteriorNpcs ports RMBLayout's non-zero-FactionID rule (RMBLayout.cs:366-378, 442-454: SetRMBPeopleData + AddComponent<StaticNPC> + SetupIndividualStaticNPC on every exterior flat with FactionID != 0), but its only importer is test/names.test.js; neither exterior host reads flat factionIDs at all (grep of exterior.js/world.js: zero hits). Known open gap: Port-Ledger.md:338 records it and test/audit18_bible_docs.test.js:334-342 pins the no-caller state (the pin restates the port).
confirmed.consequence: No exterior static NPC (factioned town flats) is ever an activation/talk/quest target outside; clicking one falls through as scenery, and quests binding individuals at exterior flats cannot land.

verify.reason: collectExteriorNpcs (exteriorNpcs.js:12-14) correctly ports RMBLayout.cs:365-378's non-zero-FactionID rule, but grep of exterior.js/world.js for 'factionID' returns zero hits; only test/names.test.js imports it. test/audit18_bible_docs.test.js:337-338 pins the Port-Ledger.md line documenting this exact known no-caller gap, confirming it, not refuting.

confirmed.title: IsChildNPCData is unported; isChildNPC is read in three places and written nowhere
confirmed.claim: DFU StaticNPC.IsChildNPCData (:342-350) flags children by IsChildNPCTexture(archive, record) or factionID == 514, gating quest offers (TalkManager.cs:755-770) and the work pool (:2842). The port has no equivalent: grep of src/ shows isChildNPC/isChild only read (worldModes.js:979,1366 pass !!pn.isChildNPC; npcSession.js:466,653) and never written, and staticNpc.js carries neither the 514 constant nor the child texture table. The flag is constant false.
confirmed.consequence: A child NPC in a castle can pass the isCastleNpcOfferingQuest door and offer quests where DFU excludes children from both questor arms; the work-pool child exclusion is inert.

verify.reason: DFU gates both questor arms on IsChildNPC (TalkManager.cs:755,769 -> StaticNPC.cs:342-350: texture table or factionID==514). Port reads isChildNPC/isChild at worldModes.js:979,1366 and npcSession.js:466,653 but writes it nowhere - pn never carries it, staticNpc.js has neither the 514 constant nor a child-texture table, so it's always false and the !isChildNPC guards (npcSession.js:468,472) never exclude a child. audit24_onehome.test.js:225 pins the always-false `!!pn.isChildNPC` shape verbatim.

confirmed.title: Bow shots always use RangedAttack1 records; HasRangedAttack2 mobiles should use records 25-29
confirmed.claim: DFU picks the bow state: RangedAttack1 only if (HasRangedAttack1 && !HasRangedAttack2), else RangedAttack2 (EnemyMotor.cs:594-597); GetStateAnims maps RangedAttack2 to RangedAttack2Anims records 25-29 (DaggerfallMobileUnit.cs:840-841; EnemyBasics.cs:103-113). The port has a single 'ranged' state always returning RANGED_ATTACK1_ANIMS records 20-24 (mobileUnit.js:120), and hosts key one rangedStriking flag. Rows 130 (Battlemage) and 133 (Nightblade) carry hasRangedAttack2:true plus castsMagic (enemyBasics.js:2103, :2293), so hasBowAttack is true and their bow shots draw records 20-24 - which for these hasSpellAnimation rows are the SPELL-casting records.
confirmed.consequence: A Battlemage or Nightblade shooting its bow renders its spell-casting sprite animation instead of its bow animation (archive 489/490 records 20-24 vs 25-29); the arrow still fires on the -1 marker.

verify.reason: C#: EnemyMotor.cs:594-597 picks RangedAttack2 when HasRangedAttack2; DaggerfallMobileUnit.cs:840-841 maps it to EnemyBasics.RangedAttack2Anims (records 25-29, EnemyBasics.cs:103-109), distinct from RangedAttack1Anims (20-24). JS: mobileUnit.js:120 always returns RANGED_ATTACK1_ANIMS for state 'ranged'; no RANGED_ATTACK2_ANIMS exists in src/. enemyBasics.js rows '130'/'133' (Battlemage/Nightblade, lines 2094-2103/2288-2293) have hasRangedAttack2+hasSpellAnimation=true, so bow shot renders same records as spell cast. No pin covers this.

confirmed.title: Bow-band shots and spell casts not suppressed during knockback (CanAct chain incomplete)
confirmed.claim: DFU KnockbackMovement sets CanAct=false while KnockbackSpeed>0 (EnemyMotor.cs:317) and TakeAction runs only under `if (CanAct)` (:171-172), so DoRangedAttack (:469 - the 1/32 bow and 1/40 spell rolls) and DoTouchSpell (:473) never run mid-knockback; the Hurt state also counts as IsPlayingOneShot (Base/MobileUnit.cs:153-168), blocking the rolls at :587. The port models only the giveUpTimer part of CanAct: the band arm (enemyAttack.js:127-134) and both EnemyCaster branches (enemyCasting.js:110-130) keep running while ai.knockbackSpeed>0; hosts gate only paralysis/hostility (dungeonContext.js:2290/2312, exteriorFoes.js:294/299). Melee correctly keeps running (CanAct-independent in DFU).
confirmed.consequence: For the ~0.2-0.5s knockback window after each solid player hit, a port archer can loose its 1/32 bow shot and a caster can cast touch/ranged spells; DFU enemies cannot act at all during knockback - ranged foes fight back through hit-stun.

verify.reason: C#: KnockbackMovement sets CanAct=false whenever KnockbackSpeed>0 (EnemyMotor.cs:272-317); TakeAction (incl. DoRangedAttack:469/DoTouchSpell:473) runs only `if(CanAct)` (:171-172). JS: enemyAttack.js:127-136 rolls bow shot with no knockbackSpeed check; enemyCasting.js update (103-132) likewise none. Hosts dungeonContext.js:2290/2312 and exteriorFoes.js:294/299 gate calls only on paralysis/hostility, never knockbackSpeed. No contradicting pin (checked audit24_characters/wave32/wave33, which only pin the paralysis half).

confirmed.title: Detour override reordered ahead of DoRangedAttack in the decision chain
confirmed.claim: DFU TakeAction calls DoRangedAttack at :469 and DoTouchSpell at :473 BEFORE the `if (avoidObstaclesTimer > 0) AttemptMove(...)` detour arm at :481-484, so an in-band shooter with sight+detection stands off and shoots even while a detour timer runs (the timer just decays). The port's _classicTick takes the detour arm first (enemyMotor.js:943-951) and only then calls _doRangedAttack (:956); its comment miscites :480-484 as "TakeAction's FIRST branch". test/audit24_wave35.test.js:113-114 pins this ordering ("the detour override first of all") - the pin restates the port, not the C#, which puts the detour after both attack calls.
confirmed.consequence: For up to 0.75s after an obstacle/fall probe fires, an archer or ranged caster inside the 6-51.2 band with the target in sight keeps walking its detour instead of standing off as DFU does; shots still roll from the attack component, so it shoots on the move.

verify.reason: C#: TakeAction calls DoRangedAttack(:469)/DoTouchSpell(:473), both return-early on success, BEFORE the detour arm at :481-484. JS: `_classicTick` checks `if(detouring)` first (enemyMotor.js:943, returns 944-951) then `_doRangedAttack` (:956) - reversed order; the port's own comment (940-941) misdescribes this as DFU's 'FIRST branch'. test/audit24_wave35.test.js:113-114 only string-matches the port's own source order ('detour override first of all'), never checking real C# line order - so it's confirming evidence, not a refutation.

confirmed.title: searchMult not reset when GiveUpTimer expires (or while pacified)
confirmed.claim: DFU HandleNoAction resets searchMult=0 on ANY of its three arms - target null, GiveUpTimer <= 0, or PredictedTargetPos sentinel (EnemyMotor.cs:357-366, searchMult=0 at :362) - every FixedUpdate. The port resets it only on the predictedTargetPos===null arm (enemyMotor.js:935); the gave-up arm at :931 (`!detected && giveUpTimer <= 0`) returns without touching searchMult, and a pacified foe skips _classicTick entirely (:1039) so no arm runs. The stale ramp is only cleared later by _getDestination's clear-path arm (:869).
confirmed.consequence: A foe that ramped its search (searchMult up to 10) then gave up resumes a later non-clear-path pursuit aiming up to 10 units past the last-known position instead of at it, walking somewhere DFU's freshly-reset foe would not.

verify.reason: C#: HandleNoAction (EnemyMotor.cs:357-366) resets searchMult=0 on all 3 arms (target null, GiveUpTimer<=0, sentinel), every FixedUpdate. JS: enemyMotor.js:931 (gave-up arm) does not reset searchMult; only line 935 (sentinel arm) and line 869 (clear-path in _getDestination) do. `_classicTick` (holding both arms) only runs `if(!paralyzed&&!knocked&&isHostile)` (line 1039), so a pacified/knocked foe skips both. Stale searchMult is consumed as an offset in the search branch (878-884), matching the claimed consequence.

confirmed.title: Touch casts gated on the attack machine being Idle; DFU DoTouchSpell has no one-shot gate
confirmed.claim: DFU's DoTouchSpell condition (EnemyMotor.cs:621-623) has no isPlayingOneShot term; the only one-shot early-out above it in TakeAction is OneShotPauseActionsWhilePlaying (:465), true only for SeducerTransform states (Base/MobileUnit.cs:174-184). So a DFU foe whose melee timer is 0 mid-swing casts the touch spell, ChangeEnemyState(Spell) cutting the swing. The port adds `idle` (attack.machine.state === 'Idle') to the touch arm (enemyCasting.js:107, :110), skipping the cast until the swing ends. Reachable when ResetMeleeTimer floors to 0: 1500 - 50*(level-10) + 450*(reflexes-2) <= 0, i.e. player level ~22+ at low reflexes, ~40 at average.
confirmed.consequence: Against high-level players, a touch-caster in melee range delays its cast by up to a full swing (~0.5-1s) and its interrupted melee blow lands where DFU would have cancelled it into the spell.

verify.reason: C#: DoTouchSpell (EnemyMotor.cs:621-623) has no one-shot term; TakeAction's only one-shot gate (:465, OneShotPauseActionsWhilePlaying) is SeducerTransform-only (MobileUnit.cs:174-183); ChangeEnemyState (MobileUnit.cs:137-147) switches unconditionally, interrupting a swing. ResetMeleeTimer (EnemyAttack.cs:114-131) floors to 0 at level ~22+(low reflexes)/~40(avg), matching claim's math. JS: enemyCasting.js:107,110 adds `idle=attack.machine.state==='Idle'` as an extra required term DFU lacks. No contradicting pin found.

confirmed.title: GiveUpTimer frozen during paralysis/knockback; DFU UpdateTimers runs before the CanAct gate
confirmed.claim: DFU UpdateTimers runs unconditionally every FixedUpdate, before `if (CanAct) TakeAction` (EnemyMotor.cs:170-172): detection refills GiveUpTimer to 200 (:419-420) and it decrements per classic tick while undetected (:423-424) even for a paralyzed or knocked-back foe (HandleParalysis/KnockbackMovement only clear CanAct). The port's refill/decrement lives inside _classicTick (enemyMotor.js:929-930), which is skipped while paralyzed or knocked (:1039 `if (!paralyzed && !knocked && this.isHostile)`), so the timer freezes for the whole paralysis.
confirmed.consequence: A paralyzed foe whose player hides does not run down its 12.5s give-up window during the paralysis; when it wakes it resumes blind pursuit where DFU's foe would already have given up and stopped.

verify.reason: C#: FixedUpdate calls UpdateTimers unconditionally (EnemyMotor.cs:170) before `if(CanAct) TakeActionHandler()` (:171-172); UpdateTimers (:389-425) refills/decrements GiveUpTimer with no paralysis/knockback/CanAct check. JS: the refill/decrement (enemyMotor.js:929-930) lives inside `_classicTick`, gated `if(!paralyzed&&!knocked&&isHostile)` (line 1039) - frozen during paralysis/knockback. No other giveUpTimer writer exists besides `_classicTick` and the unrelated hostility-seed at line 563. No contradicting pin found.

confirmed.title: Billboard anim frame not reset to 0 on idle/move state switch
confirmed.claim: DFU MobilePersonBillboard.SetIdle (:291-313) resets currentFrame = 0 and animTimer = 1 on every idle<->move transition, so each state starts at frame 0. The port's MobilePerson.update (mobilePerson.js:245-256) keeps one monotonically increasing this.frame and this._timer across state changes and takes frame % n, so a transition starts at an arbitrary phase of the new record's cycle.
confirmed.consequence: A townsperson stopping to face the player (or resuming walking) starts the idle/walk cycle at a random frame instead of frame 0 - a small visible animation-phase divergence.

verify.reason: DFU MobilePersonBillboard.SetIdle (MobilePersonBillboard.cs:291-313) resets currentFrame=0/animTimer=1 on every idle<->move transition, gated by MobilePersonMotor.Update's IsIdle checks (:232,238). Port's MobilePerson.update (mobilePerson.js:225-256) keeps one monotonic this.frame/this._timer across the same transition logic (line 226-227), only applying frame % n (251,256), never resetting. Visible animation-phase divergence confirmed.

confirmed.title: place() marks the spawn tile Occupied; DFU never flags a spawn tile
confirmed.claim: MobilePerson.place (mobilePerson.js:127-141) calls nav.setOccupied(gx, gy) on the spawn cell. In DFU nothing flags the spawn tile: SpawnAvailableMobile only positions the transform (PopulationManager.cs:150-166), GetRandomSpawnPosition only tests weight > 0 (CityNavigation.cs:512-535), InitMotor resets nav positions without setting flags (:274-283), and Occupied is only ever set on TARGET tiles in SetTargetPosition (:438-439). GetNextNavPositionWeight treats Occupied as weight 0 (:528-529), which the port mirrors, so the extra flag changes the neighbour weights other walkers see.

confirmed.title: WeakensArmor applies +5 armor in port but is a no-op in DFU (setter guard refuses positive values)
confirmed.claim: WeakensArmor's ConstantEffect calls SetDecreasedArmorValueModifier(5), but that setter (DaggerfallEntity.cs:410-416) assigns only when `amount < DecreasedArmorValueModifier`, and the modifier is cleared to 0 every DoConstantEffects pass (ClearConstantEffects, DaggerfallEntity.cs:842) — 5 < 0 is never true, so the +5 never lands and the enchantment is inert in DFU. The port's row adds WEAKENS_ARMOR_VALUE (+5) into mods.armorMod each round, which combat/formulas.js:292 adds to the wearer's armor value in the attacker's hit chance.

confirmed.title: Armor modifiers stack additively per item in port; DFU's setters are non-stacking min-sets
confirmed.claim: DFU's SetIncreasedArmorValueModifier keeps only the lowest value ('does not stack'), so any number of StrengthensArmor items (each setting -5 via StrengthensArmor.cs:63) yields exactly -5; BadReactionsFrom's SetDecreasedArmorValueModifier(-5) likewise floors at -5 across items (its ChanceToHitModifier IS additive, DaggerfallEntity.cs:418-421). The port folds these into one additive channel: each StrengthensArmor row does `mods.armorMod += -5` (enchantments.js:428) and each active BadReactionsFrom adds another -5 (:527), so two Strengthens items give -10 where DFU caps at -5.

Port enchantments.js:428-429,527 does `mods.armorMod += -5` per item into one shared field (consumed at combat/formulas.js:292), so 2 StrengthensArmor items give -10. confirmed.title: Enchantment cap off-by-one: DFU's `++count > 10` break applies 11, port slices at 10

confirmed.title: Forced (child) enchantment rows can be removed by clicking them
confirmed.claim: DFU's EnchantmentPanel_OnMouseClick only removes a panel when panel.Enchantment.ParentEnchantment == 0 ('child panels are removed by clicking on parent', EnchantmentListPicker.cs:268-271). confirmed.title: Enchanting a stacked item enchants the whole stack (no SplitStack)
confirmed.claim: DFU's EnchantButton_OnMouseClick splits one item off a stack before enchanting: 'if (selectedItem.IsAStack()) selectedItem = ...Items.SplitStack(selectedItem, 1)' (cs:752-754). confirmed.title: Cast When Used/Held/Strikes list rows print the wrong spell name

The port draws the secondary row as names[row.entry.param] (itemMakerWindow.js:390-393), where names = enchantmentParams(type) is a DENSE list-ordered array (enchantmentCatalogue.js:193-201) but entry.param for the three CastWhen* effects is the sparse classic SPELL ID (catalogue :171, stored at :233). Verified: catalogue.js:104 has 'Resist Fire' at index 9 and 'Fireball' at index 12, so names[12]='Fireball' for param 12 (Resist Fire), matching the claim exactly. Param 94 (Recall) exceeds the 34-entry array and prints blank.

confirmed.title: Enchantment lists cannot scroll; overflowing rows are invisible and unremovable
confirmed.claim: DFU's EnchantmentListPicker shows a slim scrollbar when enchantmentPanels.Count > 7 (ShowScroller, cs:244-247), narrows rows to 71 wide, and scrolls via wheel (MouseScrollUp/Down cs:180-196) and the scroller. The port's draw loop breaks at 'if (row.y + row.h > rect[3]) break' (itemMakerWindow.js:385), computes 'scrolled' and voids it (:383, :395), and neither click() (:338-344) nor input() offers any scroll path for the two lists. With rows carrying secondary names (12px + 5 gap), only 7 rows fit in the 120px rect, so an 8th+ row (reachable: up to 10 enchantments, e.g. eight Cast When Used spells) is off-panel.
confirmed.consequence: Enchantments past the seventh two-line row can be neither seen nor clicked off; DFU scrolls to them.

verify.reason: EnchantmentListPicker.cs:23 visiblePanels=7; ShowScroller (cs:245-247) plus MouseScrollUp/Down (cs:180-196) activate past 7 panels. itemMakerWindow.js rowLayout (145-154) always starts at fixed y with no scroll offset; the draw loop computes scrolled (383) then discards it (void scrolled; 395) and breaks past the rect (385); click (338-344) hit-tests with no offset either; no wheel/scroll handling exists for these lists anywhere in the file. 12px+5px rows fill exactly 7 of the 120px rect, so an 8th+ enchantment (reachable, MAX_ENCHANTMENTS=10) is unreachable to view or remove.

confirmed.title: Item rename caps at 26 characters vs DFU's TextBox default 31
confirmed.claim: DFU's rename runs through DaggerfallInputMessageBox whose TextBox default maxCharacters is 31 (TextBox.cs:26), and RenameItem itself imposes no cap (DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:1348-1354). The port's inline rename field (a recorded widget departure) stops accepting characters at 26 (itemMakerWindow.js:316: 'this.itemName.length < 26').
confirmed.consequence: Item names 27-31 characters long, legal in DFU, cannot be typed in the port's rename strip.

verify.reason: DFU's NameItemButon_OnMouseClick (DaggerfallItemMakerWindow.cs:797-806) opens `new DaggerfallInputMessageBox(uiManager, this)` - the 2-arg ctor - which never sets textBox.MaxCharacters, so it stays at TextBox.cs:26's field default of 31. The port's rename input (itemMakerWindow.js:316) gates with `this.itemName.length < 26`. No test pin exists. Confirmed nit: legal 27-31 char DFU names cannot be typed.

confirmed.title: Recipe pick partially fills the cauldron instead of refusing when ingredients are missing
confirmed.claim: DFU's AddRecipeToCauldron: if any recipe ingredient is unmatched it shows GetLocalizedText("reqIngredients") and adds NOTHING (cs:297-301); otherwise it ClearCauldron()s first, adds every ingredient, and sets nameLabel = recipeName (cs:302-308). The port's _fillFrom (potionMakerWindow.js:184-194) adds whatever gatherRecipe found (potions.js:229-239) - no missing-ingredient message, no cauldron clear (fills on top of existing contents), no name label. potions.js:224-228's comment claims DFU 'fills what it can... does not refuse', which the C# contradicts; potionmakerwindow.test.js:180-191 pins the port behavior while citing :283-309 - the pin restates the port.
confirmed.consequence: Picking a recipe while missing one herb silently loads an incomplete cauldron; mixing burns the ingredients on a useless potion, where DFU refuses with a message. Picking with leftovers in the pot also mixes them in.

verify.reason: DFU's AddRecipeToCauldron checks `recipeIngreds.ContainsValue(null)`: if true it MessageBoxes 'reqIngredients' and adds NOTHING; else ClearCauldron() then adds every ingredient. The port's _fillFrom (potionMakerWindow.js:185-194) unconditionally adds whatever gatherRecipe finds, no clear, no message. test/potionmakerwindow.test.js:178-190 pins exactly this partial-fill while citing the same C# - per doctrine this confirms the finding since my own read shows DFU refuses entirely on any missing ingredient.

confirmed.title: Mixing an empty cauldron shows the failure message instead of doing nothing
confirmed.claim: DFU's MixButton_OnMouseClick plays the click and only calls MixCauldron() 'if (cauldron.Count > 0)' (cs:396-397). The port's _mix (potionMakerWindow.js:151-169) has no emptiness guard: mixCauldron([]) hashes the empty list, matches no recipe, and the window shows the POTION_FAILED box ('The ingredients you have combined are useless.').
confirmed.consequence: Clicking MIX (or pressing M/Enter) with an empty pot pops a failure message box that DFU never shows.

verify.reason: DFU's MixButton_OnMouseClick only calls MixCauldron() inside `if (cauldron.Count > 0)`. The port's _mix (potionMakerWindow.js:151-169), wired from click():209 and input() Enter/KeyM:200, has no such guard: mixCauldron([]) returns {kind:'failed'} (potionRecipeKey([]) returns 0 early, no recipe is empty) so this.box is set to POTION_FAILED. No test covers the empty-cauldron path. Confirmed.

confirmed.title: Enchanted ingredients are not excluded from the potion maker's list
confirmed.claim: DFU's Refresh collects ingredients with 'if (item.IsIngredient && !item.IsEnchanted)' (cs:148), and the consume walk also passes allowEnchantedItem: false (cs:338, :345). The port's ingredients() (potionMakerWindow.js:125-133) filters with isIngredient(it) alone (potions.js:184 - template flag only), so an enchanted gem (mintable at the port's own item maker, which lists Gems) appears in the ingredient grid and can be added to the cauldron and consumed.
confirmed.consequence: A player can grind an enchanted ruby into a potion - and the takeOne consumption may instead burn an unenchanted one - where DFU keeps enchanted items out of the pot entirely.

verify.reason: DFU's Refresh filters ingredients with `item.IsIngredient && !item.IsEnchanted`. The port's ingredients() (potionMakerWindow.js:125-133) filters with only isIngredient(it) (template flag), never calling the port's own isEnchantedItem helper (enchantments.js:112) that other systems like repairService.js:404 do use. Gems (ingredient-flagged, e.g. Diamond id3/Turquoise id5 in potions.js's own table) are enchantable via the port's item maker. No test pin. Confirmed.

confirmed.title: Ingredient list never scrolls: this.scroll has no writer
confirmed.claim: DFU's ingredientsListScroller is a scrolling ItemListScroller (4 rows x 3 cols, cs:226-233) with scroll handling for an arbitrary ingredient count. The port initializes this.scroll = 0 (potionMakerWindow.js:113) and reads it at :216 and :234, but nothing in click() or input() ever modifies it - grep confirms those are the only three references. Only the first 12 ingredient stacks are ever shown or clickable.
confirmed.consequence: A player holding more than 12 distinct ingredient stacks (routine for an alchemist) can never see or use ingredients 13+, and recipes needing them can only be loaded via the RECIPES button.

verify.reason: DFU's ingredientsListScroller is built with scroll=true (a real VerticalScrollBar, ItemListScroller.cs:239-263), vs the cauldron's false. Grepping potionMakerWindow.js for `.scroll` gives exactly 3 hits: init at :113, reads at :216 and :234 - no writer in click() or input(). Confirmed dead state: ingredient stacks beyond the first 12 are permanently unreachable.

confirmed.title: Adding an ingredient from a stack hides the whole stack (no SplitStack)
confirmed.claim: DFU's AddToCauldron splits one unit off a stack before moving it: 'if (item.IsAStack()) item = ingredients.SplitStack(item, 1)' (cs:256-257), leaving the remainder visible and addable. The port's _addToCauldron (potionMakerWindow.js:137-141) pushes the stack OBJECT into the cauldron, and ingredients() (:125-133) removes it from the list by identity, so a stack of N elderberries vanishes entirely from the grid while one conceptual unit is in the pot; a second unit of the same stack cannot be added.
confirmed.consequence: With merged ingredient stacks (the port stacks ingredients per inventory.js:110), the remaining N-1 units are invisible and unusable while one is in the cauldron; DFU shows and offers the remainder.

verify.reason: DFU's AddToCauldron does `if (item.IsAStack()) item = ingredients.SplitStack(item, 1);` before adding, leaving the remainder visible. The port's _addToCauldron (potionMakerWindow.js:137-141) pushes the item reference directly with no split; ingredients() (:125-133) removes it from the pack list by identity, hiding the WHOLE stack. Confirmed via inventory.js's isStackable (ingredients stack) and equip.js's own SplitStack-equivalent pattern, unused here. No test exercises stackCount>1 (test helper ing() defaults n=1).

confirmed.title: Name label is set on successful mix; DFU sets it only on recipe fill
confirmed.claim: DFU's MixCauldron never touches nameLabel (cs:311-360); the label is written only by AddRecipeToCauldron ('nameLabel.Text = recipeName', cs:307) and cleared by every add/remove. The port inverts this: _mix sets this.nameLabel = result.recipe.name on success (potionMakerWindow.js:158) while _fillFrom leaves it blank (finding on :184 above). potionmakerwindow.test.js:136 pins the port's mix-time label.
confirmed.consequence: The bottom-left name label shows the potion name after mixing (it stays blank in DFU) and stays blank after a recipe fill (where DFU shows the recipe name).

verify.reason: DFU: MixCauldron (cs:311-360) never touches nameLabel; only AddRecipeToCauldron sets nameLabel.Text=recipeName on fill (cs:307); Add/RemoveFromCauldron clear it (cs:255,268). Port inverts: potionMakerWindow.js:158 sets nameLabel in _mix() (MixCauldron's port); _fillFrom (:184-194, AddRecipeToCauldron's port) never sets it, only clears via _addToCauldron. test:136 pins the port's mix-time label, confirming the divergence.

confirmed.title: Potion maker gold label wired to coins only, not GetGoldAmount
confirmed.claim: DFU's potion maker label reads GameManager.Instance.PlayerEntity.GetGoldAmount() (cs:138), which is goldPieces + letters of credit (PlayerEntity.cs:1313-1316). confirmed.title: Sort-by-cost applies the lycanthropy free-cast quirk; DFU sorts by real cost
confirmed.claim: DFU's SortSpellsPointCost orders by the raw CalculateTotalEffectCosts spell-point cost (DaggerfallEntity.cs:743-748) with no tag check - the lycanthropy 0-display quirk lives only in PopulateSpellsList (DaggerfallSpellBookWindow.cs:264-267). confirmed.title: Spellbook scroll bar is drawn but not interactive
confirmed.claim: DFU's VerticalScrollBar supports thumb dragging (Update, cs:104-128) and click-above/below-thumb paging by displayUnits (MouseClick, cs:140-148), wired to the list via OnScroll (DaggerfallSpellBookWindow.cs:371, :794-797). The port draws the thumb (spellbookWindow.js:784-789) but click() (:649-705) has no branch for SPELLBOOK_RECTS.scrollBar - a click there falls through to 'return true' with no effect, and there is no drag path.

verify.reason: VerticalScrollBar.cs:101-150 supports thumb drag (Update) and click-paging (MouseClick). confirmed.title: Spell maker ignores allowedTargets/allowedElements restrictions from chosen effects
confirmed.claim: DFU restricts target and element to what the chosen effects allow: SetSpellTarget returns early when '(allowedTargets & targetType) == TargetTypes.None' (cs:499-501), SetSpellElement likewise (cs:527-530), and UpdateAllowedButtons recomputes allowedTargets as the INTERSECTION of each effect's Properties.AllowedTargets and allowedElements as magic-only union (cs:563-601), forcing the selection back to the first allowed value. The port's _inputMain cycles rangeType and element freely through all five values (spellMakerWindow.js:187-190) and no allowedTargets/allowedElements state exists anywhere in src/ (grep confirms).
confirmed.consequence: The port will price and inscribe combinations DFU forbids - e.g. an 'Area at Range' spell from a caster-only effect - producing spells with wrong target semantics and costs that classic/DFU can never mint.

verify.reason: SetSpellTarget/SetSpellElement (cs:488-530) early-return outside allowedTargets/allowedElements; UpdateAllowedButtons (cs:561-660) intersects each effect's AllowedTargets/AllowedElements and resets the selection. Port's spellMakerWindow.js:187-190 cycles rangeType/element by plain modulo with no restriction; grep confirms no such state exists in src/, and spellMaker.js buildCustomSpell/validateSpellPurchase (:113-170) apply no check at purchase either.

confirmed.title: envAttack skips Receive(Attack) on doors; DFU fires the door's action record before bashing
confirmed.claim: DFU WeaponEnvDamage (WeaponManager.cs:460-464) calls action.Receive(player, Attack) on ANY hit object with a DaggerfallAction - including an action door (one GameObject, both components) - and THEN (:467-471) calls actionDoor.AttemptBash(true). Port envAttack (weaponRig.js:159-162): a door branch does attemptBash and returns; only non-doors get receive('Attack'). So an Attack/MultiTrigger-flagged door record (Castle Wayrest doors are MultiTrigger, DaggerfallActionDoor.cs:263 comment) never fires on a weapon hit; the bash path's _execOwnAction passes only the 'Door' trigger, which those flags reject. test/weaponrig.test.js:83 pins the port's behavior, restating the port.
confirmed.consequence: Attacking an Attack/MultiTrigger action door (e.g. Castle Wayrest DoorText doors whose record runs the trespass check) never fires its record in the port; DFU fires it on every weapon hit.

verify.reason: WeaponManager.cs:457-472: action.Receive(player,Attack) fires unconditionally on any DaggerfallAction (:460-464), then AttemptBash runs separately if DaggerfallActionDoor is also present (:467-471); both can coexist on one door. Port's envAttack (weaponRig.js:159-162): doors get attemptBash+return, skipping receive('Attack'). attemptBash's fire path gates on 'Door' trigger (actionSystem.js:692-699) while Attack/MultiTrigger map to Attack/Direct/WalkInto, not Door (:117-119), so such records never fire either way. test/weaponrig.test.js:80-89 pins this skip.

confirmed.title: Dungeon castle/special-area ambient (0.58) unported - castle blocks render at 0.12
confirmed.claim: PlayerAmbientLight.UpdateAmbientLight (:84-92) selects CastleAmbientLight (0.58) inside dungeon castle blocks, SpecialAreaLight (0.58) in special areas, DungeonAmbientLight (0.12) otherwise. The port exports only DUNGEON_AMBIENT [0.12,0.12,0.12] (dungeonLights.js:14) and both dungeon hosts apply it unconditionally (worldModes.js:2747, dungeon.js:247). The castle predicate exists live in the port (dungeonContext.js:2012 castleBlockAt, used for music and water sounds, exposed at :2524) but is never consulted for ambient - a law input computed and thrown away at the seam.
confirmed.consequence: Non-hostile castle wings (Castle Daggerfall/Wayrest/Sentinel) render at ambient 0.12 instead of 0.58 - about 5x darker than DFU; the brighten-in-castle-block behavior is absent.

verify.reason: PlayerAmbientLight.UpdateAmbientLight (PlayerAmbientLight.cs:84-92) picks CastleAmbientLight/SpecialAreaLight (0.58) vs DungeonAmbientLight (0.12) via IsPlayerInsideDungeonCastle/SpecialArea. Port's DUNGEON_AMBIENT (dungeonLights.js:14) is applied unconditionally in worldModes.js:2745 and dungeon.js:247; the live castleBlockAt/inCastle predicate (dungeonContext.js:2012,2078,2524) feeds only music/ambientEffects, never lighting.

confirmed.title: Door close sound fires at swing start; DFU plays it when the close completes
confirmed.claim: DFU Close() (:311-332) starts the reverse tween and plays NO sound; CloseSound plays in OnCompleteClose (:339-346), after the 1.5 s swing, just before the collider re-solidifies. The port's _closeDoor (actionSystem.js:656-657) emits onDoorState(o, false) at close START and both hosts play the clip immediately (dungeonContext.js:199-202, interiorContext.js:51-54). Open-side timing matches DFU (sound at open start, :296-302 vs actionSystem.js:645).
confirmed.consequence: Every door close is audible ~1.5 s early - the shut sound plays while the door is still swinging instead of when it lands closed as in DFU.

verify.reason: DaggerfallActionDoor.Close (:311-332) plays no sound; CloseSound plays in OnCompleteClose (:339-346) after the tween. Port's _closeDoor (actionSystem.js:653-660) fires onDoorState(o,false) at close START; both hosts (dungeonContext.js:199-202, interiorContext.js:51-54) play the clip immediately. No completion callback plays sound (checked _tickDoor's settle branch, actionSystem.js:964-973 - collider only).

confirmed.title: Port persists activationCount across save/load; DFU resets it to 0
confirmed.claim: SerializableActionObject (:55-88) persists only position/rotation/currentState/tween percentage; SerializableActionDoor (:67-101) adds lock and FailedSkillLevel. Neither serializes DaggerfallAction.activationCount, and the scene rebuilds on load, so every counter restarts at 0 in DFU. The port saves it for every object (actionSystem.js:830-832) and restores it (:858-859). Save-relevant state semantics are in the byte-exact doctrine list.
confirmed.consequence: After loading, DFU re-shows a DoorText door's text and holds it shut on first click, and restarts Hurt21's every-20th phase; the port does neither, so trap cadence and first-click door behavior diverge after any save/load.

verify.reason: Neither SerializableActionObject (:55-88) nor SerializableActionDoor (:67-101) save/restore DaggerfallAction.activationCount (DaggerfallAction.cs:44, gates DoorText@1 :870 and Hurt21 %20 :725), so a reloaded scene resets it to 0. Port persists+restores it (actionSystem.js:830-832,858-859); test/action.test.js:316-327 pins this as deliberate but cites no DFU serializer carrying the field - restates the divergence, doesn't refute it.

confirmed.title: LightningPlayer slots are always 2 frames; DFU's skipped flash is a 1-frame slot
confirmed.claim: DFU PlayLightningEffects (:367-382): per flash, `if (Random.value < 0.6) { on; yield; }` then unconditionally off + yield - a skipped flash consumes ONE frame, a lit one two. The port (weather.js:169-179) always spends two frames per slot, and its comment claims parity with 'the coroutine's WaitForEndOfFrame pairs'. Also DFU re-arms the next 4-35 s wait at strike time (:146-152), while the port re-arms after the sequence ends (:176-179).
confirmed.consequence: Storm flash sequences run up to ~2x the frames of DFU (a 20-30 flash roll is ~0.3-0.5 s longer at 60 fps) and successive strikes drift slightly later; visual timing only.

verify.reason: AmbientEffectsPlayer.PlayLightningEffects (:359-368): skipped flash = 1 WaitForEndOfFrame, lit flash = 2; StartWaiting() re-arms immediately after launching the coroutine (:146-152, strike time). Port's LightningPlayer.tick (weather.js:166-179) always spends 2 frames/slot and re-arms only when the whole sequence ends (line 176-179). test/weather.test.js:106-110 pins the always-2-frame design, restating rather than refuting.

confirmed.title: failedSkillLevel omitted from save snapshot (in-code FLAGGED gap, confirmed)
confirmed.claim: SerializableActionDoor saves lockpickFailedSkillLevel (:77) and restores it (:99-101), so DFU's lockpick retry gate (FailedSkillLevel == live skill, DaggerfallActionDoor.cs:157) survives save/load. The port's collectSaveData (actionSystem.js:829-837) omits failedSkillLevel and restore never sets it, resetting it to 0 on load. The port already flags this at addDoor (:460-467, 'FLAGGED, a live gap'). Reported to confirm the flag is accurate - both sides read this session.
confirmed.consequence: A player who failed a pick at their current skill can save+load and immediately retry the same lock; DFU blocks the retry until the live skill changes.

verify.reason: SerializableActionDoor.cs:77,99-101 save/restore FailedSkillLevel, preserving DFU's lockpick retry gate (:157) across load. Port's collectSaveData/restoreSaveData (actionSystem.js:825-864) omit failedSkillLevel; the port's own addDoor comment (:460-467) already flags this as a live gap - confirmed accurate by reading both sides.

confirmed.title: Nature scatter rect exclusion gated on pre-expansion mins; DFU re-checks the expanded rect per tile
confirmed.claim: DFU LayoutNature expands the location rect by natureClearance=4 only when the un-expanded rect has x>0 && y>0 (TerrainNature.cs:60-66), then in the tile loop re-evaluates `rect.x > 0 && rect.y > 0 && rect.Contains(tilePos)` on the EXPANDED rect (TerrainNature.cs:124) - so when expansion pushes xMin or yMin to <= 0, DFU disables the containment test entirely and scatters nature inside the location footprint. The port (terrainNature.js:72-79) builds the rect when the PRE-expansion mins are > 0 and then applies containment unconditionally at line 112, never re-checking the expanded mins.
confirmed.consequence: For a location whose pre-clearance rect min on either axis lies in (0, 4] (only possible for 8-block-wide/tall locations, since the tile origin is 0 only then), DFU places nature billboards over the town footprint while the port suppresses them - a visible foliage difference at large walled cities with narrow edge blend space.

verify.reason: TerrainNature.cs:60-66: rect.xMin/xMax +-= clearance mutates the underlying x/y fields (Unity Rect semantics); the tile-loop reject at :124 re-tests rect.x>0&&rect.y>0 against the EXPANDED value, so a pre-expansion min in (0,4] disables containment. Port (terrainNature.js:72-79) gates rect-building on PRE-expansion mins only, then at :112 tests mere truthiness of rect with no re-check - always excludes where DFU sometimes wouldn't.

confirmed.title: Quest item use never sets useClicked - ItemUsedDo quests cannot advance
confirmed.claim: DFU UseItem sets questItem.UseClicked=true on a use click and shows the item's UsedMessageID popup (InventoryWindow.cs:1681-1700); the port's ItemUsedDo action is live and polls item.useClicked (systems/quest/actions.js:1028-1038), but no site in src/ ever sets useClicked=true - quest/item.js:74 initializes it false, useItem() only attaches a 'questItem:true' rider (useItem.js:190-195), and nativeInventory._useResult ignores that rider. isParchment/isClothing (useItem.js:77-79), ported verbatim for exactly this DFU block's parchment/clothing exception, have zero callers.
confirmed.consequence: Any quest using '<item> used do <task>' or 'used saying' stalls forever - using the quest item does nothing, the task never starts, and quest letters' used-message popup never shows.

verify.reason: DFU sets questItem.UseClicked=true at DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1683 (!UseClicked && ActionWatching); ItemUsedDo.cs:65 polls it, ported at actions.js:1027-1037. grep 'useClicked' src/ shows only quest/item.js:74/312 (init/deserialize) - no production write ever sets it true. nativeInventory.js:333-375 _useResult never reads useItem.js:295's questItem rider, so pop-to-HUD/UseClicked never fires. test/questactions.test.js:631 manually sets useClicked=true to bypass the gap, confirming no end-to-end pin exists. isParchment/isClothing also zero callers.

confirmed.title: Exterior static NPCs are inert - collectExteriorNpcs has no caller
confirmed.claim: DFU RMBLayout adds a StaticNPC behaviour plus QuestMachine.SetupIndividualStaticNPC to every exterior RMB flat with FactionID != 0 (RMBLayout.cs:370-377 and :446-453), making them clickable talk/quest targets. The port translated the filter (collectExteriorNpcs, exteriorNpcs.js:12-14) but no host calls it: world.js:455-457 and exterior.js:312 add all block flats as plain billboards via addFlat, and the only static-NPC talk paths (worldModes.js:978/1365 talkToStaticNPC) come from collectInteriorPeople.

verify.reason: RMBLayout.cs:366-378/442-454 adds StaticNPC+SetupIndividualStaticNPC when FactionID!=0. collectExteriorNpcs' only caller anywhere is test/names.test.js - zero production callers. world.js:455-456 and exterior.js:312 route all flats through addFlat/flatGroups as plain billboards, no factionID branch. worldModes.js:844-867 explicitly says the click seam is interior-only ('the only host that builds a building interior, so it is the only one with StaticNPCs to click'); openStaticNpc is driven solely by collectInteriorPeople (interiorContext.js:199), never collectExteriorNpcs.

confirmed.title: Alliance/war/ruler mutators ported but the 38-day conditions update never calls them

Wars/alliances/rulers stay frozen either way.

confirmed.title: Travel map hasShip hardwired false - ship ownership and knight free-ship perk unwired
confirmed.claim: DFU computes hasShip = DaggerfallBankManager.OwnsShip || GuildManager.FreeShipTravel() (TravelPopUp.cs:219). The port ships both halves - banking.ownsShip is live in worldModes.js:1231 and KnightlyOrder rank-6 freeShipTravel is ported (guildServices.js:336, zero callers) - but buildTravelMapWindow passes the literal `hasShip: false` (world.js:1728, with a stale 'a SHIP still has no ownership state' comment) and neither call site (world.js:1692/:1702) overrides it, so calculateTripCost's !hasShip arm (travel.js:86) always charges.

confirmed.title: Class enemies get no enemy-group bit; DFU maps careerIndex (mobileType-128) into the monster table
confirmed.claim: Port enemyGroupOf/entityFlags (:186, :206) look up ENEMY_GROUP_BIT[mobileType], so class enemies (>=128) get None; the comment at :194-198 claims that is DFU behaviour. It is not: GetEnemyEntityEnemyGroup switches on e.CareerIndex (FormulaHelper.cs:2752), and for EnemyClass careerIndex = ID-128 (EnemyEntity.cs:293), colliding into the MonsterCareers cases: Mage(0=Rat)=Animals, Burglar(7=Orc)=Humanoid, Barbarian(15)=Undead, Knight(17=Zombie)=Undead, CityWatch(18=Ghost)=Undead. PlayerGPS.GetEntityFlags:785-804, PacifyEffect.cs:132 and DispelUndead.cs:50-58 consume it with no class gate. Pin test/pacify.test.js:55-62 restates the port; port consumer effects.js:1212.
confirmed.consequence: In DFU, Pacify Animal calms a class Mage, Pacify Undead calms a Knight/Barbarian/City Watch, Dispel Undead can destroy nearby Knights, and class enemies carry group bits in the nearby-object flags (Detect scans, Near-X enchantments). In the port none of these ever touch a class enemy.

confirmed.title: Large HUD branch drops the breath bar DFU keeps enabled
confirmed.claim: DaggerfallHUD.cs:203 sets breathBar.Enabled = ShowBreathBar every frame, and the large-HUD force-off block (:214-220) disables only vitals, compass and interactionModeIcon - the breath bar stays on and draws while the large HUD is up. The port's drawHud large branch (hud.js:284-293) draws drawHudLarge, the crosshair and the spell rows then returns at line 292, so the breath-bar draw at hud.js:313-323 is unreachable; drawHudLarge (hudLarge.js:324-371) draws no breath bar either. The port's own comment at hud.js:279 ('the CROSSHAIR and the breath bar stay') states the DFU law it then fails to implement; no test pins the omission.
confirmed.consequence: With GUI/LargeHUD on, a player swimming underwater gets no breath bar at all - no drowning warning until damage starts.

confirmed.title: EnableVitalsIndicators loss/gain bars unported; default-on DFU behavior missing
confirmed.claim: HUDVitals.cs adds six indicator bars when EnableVitalsIndicators is true (:99-115): smoothed loss trails (colors :41-46) and gain bars, driven by VitalsChangeDetector events (:290-312) and Cycle() (:282-287); only when false does it take SynchronizeImmediately (:211-214). Port hud.js:300-310 draws only the three plain instant bars - the setting-false path - and nothing in src/ reads GUI/EnableVitalsIndicators (grep: only settingsDefaults.js:106 where it defaults "True", settingsMap.js:162, settingsCopy.js:118, which surface it in the settings screen). Not recorded in hud.js, UI-Arc.md U1, or anywhere else.
confirmed.consequence: The damage/heal trail DFU shows by default on the HUD bars never appears, and the surfaced 'Vitals Indicators' toggle does nothing.

confirmed.title: SwapHealthAndFatigueColors setting has no consumer; toggle is inert
confirmed.claim: HUDVitals.LoadAssets (:181-198) swaps the health and fatigue bar art (MAIN03I0/MAIN04I0) and their indicator colors when Settings.SwapHealthAndFatigueColors is true. The port's loadHud (hud.js:188-190) maps MAIN03I0->health and MAIN04I0->fatigue unconditionally, and no file in src/ reads the key (grep: only settingsDefaults.js:95, settingsCopy.js:137, settingsMap.js:205, which surface it as 'Swap Bar Colours' on the settings screen's Accessibility page). hudLarge.js:349-352 reuses the same unswapped art. Not recorded as a departure anywhere.
confirmed.consequence: Turning on 'Swap Bar Colours' (DFU's red-health/green-fatigue accessibility swap) changes nothing on either HUD.

confirmed.title: Book layout merges Text tokens into one row and centers the justify-terminated line, unlike CreateBookLabels
confirmed.claim: DFU CreateBookLabels creates a SEPARATE label per Text token (:254), each its own row via LayoutBookLabels (y += label.Size.y, :326), with alignment applied only to labels created AFTER a justify token (:241-245). The port (bookReader.js:97-110) concatenates a line's Text tokens into ONE row and applies JustifyCenter retroactively (current.center=true, :103). For Text('A'),0xFD,Text('B'),NewLine (the shape the port's test PAGE1 models), DFU renders 'A' Left and 'B' Center on two rows; the port renders one centered row 'AB'. test/books.test.js:140-153 pins the port (['CenteredOffset line', true]) while citing the C# - the pin restates the port.
confirmed.consequence: Classic books using 0xFD line terminators (centered title pages, poems) render consecutive centered lines run together on one over-wide row, with centering shifted one line versus DFU.

confirmed.title: shouldClose drops the unconditional Escape close, making quest and infection videos unskippable
confirmed.claim: DFU closes the vid window on 'endOnAnyKey && AnyKeyDown || GetBackButtonDown() || EndOfFile && Playing' (:140-142); GetBackButtonDown is Escape keydown (InputManager.cs:1065-1067), checked OUTSIDE the endOnAnyKey gate, so EndOnAnyKey=false videos (PlayVideo.cs:78, VampirismInfection.cs:126/136, LycanthropyInfection.cs:114) still skip on Escape. The port's shouldClose (videoPlayer.js:234-236) is '(endOnAnyKey && anyKeyDown) || (endOfFile && playing)' with no back-button arm, and shared.js:936 passes endOnAnyKey:false for infection videos - its comment even asserts they 'cannot be skipped', misreading DFU.
confirmed.consequence: The vampirism/lycanthropy dream and turning videos and quest PlayVideo actions cannot be skipped with Escape in the port; in DFU Escape always closes the video window.

confirmed.title: Settings dialog treats ANY click as the affirmative - drawn Cancel/Keep It buttons confirm on click
confirmed.claim: click() with a dialog open (settingsWindow.js:469-475) runs 'this.dialog = null; if (d.onYes) d.onYes(); else if (d.buttons?.[0]?.id === 'yes') this._commit(d.key, 'False')' with NO hit-test of the dialog's buttons, while _drawDialog (:639-646) renders distinct buttons including refusals ('Cancel' on Reset Everything :460, 'Keep It' on the ShowOptionsAtStart lock-out :302). Only the keyboard path (:419-431) treats Escape as refusal. So a pointer click on the drawn Cancel button - or anywhere - executes onYes (resetToDefaults :461) or commits 'False'. test/settingsUI.test.js:308-312 pins click-anywhere-runs-the-action, restating the port.
confirmed.consequence: A mouse/touch player tapping 'Cancel' on Reset Everything wipes every settings override; tapping 'Keep It' disables the settings-at-start option anyway. No pointer path can decline a dialog.
